name: Japchae - Korean Glass Noodle Stir Fry
why: A colourful Korean classic that's equal parts stir-fry and noodle salad — sweet potato glass noodles tossed with vibrant vegetables and marinated beef in a savoury-sweet sesame sauce. Perfect for Martin's Korean cuisine exploration, and the 'toss-in-a-bowl' technique is a fun new approach.
author: Henry
ingredients: 300g boneless beef short ribs (or scotch fillet/rib eye, tenderised)
1 1/2 tbsp toasted sesame oil (for noodle dressing)
1 onion, peeled, halved, sliced into 6mm wedges
3 green onion stems, cut into 5cm lengths (white & green parts separated)
200g fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, sliced 5mm thick
1 red bell pepper, cut into 0.5cm slices

steps: Cut beef into strips ~5mm thick, 1cm wide, 5cm long. If using short ribs, trim excess fat and slice meat off the bone, then cut into thin strips.
Place beef in a bowl. Add 2 tsp soy sauce, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tsp minced garlic, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Mix well and set aside to marinate for 15-20 minutes while you prepare everything else.
Mix the noodle dressing in a very large mixing bowl: 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tsp sugar, 1 1/2 tbsp toasted sesame oil, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Cook sweet potato noodles per packet directions (normally 8 minutes in boiling water). Drain, briefly rinse under tap water, then shake off excess water.
Add the drained noodles directly into the sauce bowl. Toss to coat evenly with the dressing.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat. Add onion, white parts of green onions, and shiitake mushrooms. Sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 2 minutes until mushrooms just start to soften. Transfer to the noodle bowl.

Using the same pan on high heat, add 1 tbsp oil. Cook carrot and bell pepper for 1 1/2 minutes, constantly stirring. Add spinach and remaining 1/2 tsp salt, cook 30 seconds until just wilted. Transfer to the noodle bowl.
In the same pan, heat the final 1 tbsp oil on high heat. Add the marinated beef and cook for 1 1/2 minutes until very lightly golden and just cooked through — do not overcook.
Add the cooked beef to the noodle bowl. Add most of the sesame seeds (reserve some for topping).
Toss everything together thoroughly — toss, toss, toss until all ingredients are well combined and coated in sauce.
Transfer to a serving bowl, sprinkle with remaining sesame seeds and the green parts of the green onions.
Serve warm, not piping hot. This dish tastes great at room temperature too.

pro_tips: The key to great Japchae is high heat and speed — cook each vegetable batch quickly so they stay crisp-tender, not soggy. Don't crowd the pan.

Sweet potato noodles (dangmyeon) have a unique slippery, chewy texture you won't find with regular noodles. They're available in the Asian aisle of most large supermarkets. Glass noodles (clear vermicelli) work as a substitute in a pinch.
